ai.title: Kimi tool call compat layer
ai.summary: Added `kimi-tool-compat.ts` to inject `id` fields into tool declarations and `name` fields into tool-result messages for `moonshotai/*` models. This satisfies Kimi's strict OpenAI-compatible schema requirements which reject standard Chat Completions payloads lacking these fields. The compatibility layer is applied in `canopywave.ts` and `openrouter.ts` via `isKimiModel` checks before sending requests. Types updated in `types.ts` to include optional `tools` and `id` fields.

eli5.text: If you use the service through a provider that routes to Kimi models (the ones labeled with a moonshotai prefix), those models expect slightly different data than other providers accept. Requests sent to those models now automatically get the extra fields attached that Kimi requires; other models keep receiving their normal data. From your perspective, conversations that rely on those specific models no longer get rejected for missing those fields.

ai.title: Simplify ad response shape
ai.summary: Ad response shape simplified to `ads: AdResponse[] | null` across CLI and Web. Removed `AdVariant` ('banner' | 'choice') and single-ad `ad` field in favor of unified array. `useGravityAd` hook now returns `ads` directly; `ChoiceAdBanner` always receives array. Server API returns `{ ads: [], provider }` for empty cases via `noAdsResponse` helper. Gravity provider drops A/B variant logic and `BANNER_PLACEMENT_ID`, always using `CHOICE_PLACEMENT_IDS`. Carbon provider returns `{ ads }` without variant wrapper. Files: `cli/src/chat.tsx`, `cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts`, `web/src/app/api/v1/ads/_post.ts`, `web/src/lib/ad-providers/gravity.ts`, `web/src/lib/ad-providers/carbon.ts`, `web/src/lib/ad-providers/types.ts`.

eli5.text: When you open the app and don't have a paid subscription, a small ad banner may appear at the bottom of your screen. Previously, the system sometimes served two different layouts (a single-banner or a multi-choice design), and the code had to decide which one to show. That split has been removed: every non-subscriber now gets the same single ad array pulled from one shared pool, and the banner simply reads whatever list of ads comes back. If you look closely, the ad spot now always behaves the same way instead of occasionally switching between two slightly different presentations.

eli5.text: When you use the free or lite version of the assistant, it now uses a different AI model called Kimi K2.6 instead of the previous one. This affects everything from the main coding helper to the file finder and code reviewer, so all the free tasks you ask it to do now run through this new model. The new model has the same usage limits as the old one, you can use it for 5 sessions at a time, and each session lasts up to 12 hours. If you open the app today and use the free version, you're already using Kimi K2.6 instead of the older model.

ai.title: Dev-only localhost bypass for free mode country check
ai.summary: getFreeModeCountryAccess now accepts allowLocalhost flag, gated on NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT === 'dev'. When set, requests lacking cf-ipcountry from loopback IPs (127.x, ::1, ::ffff:127.0.0.1) or missing client IP resolve as US-allowed, skipping ipinfo/geoip. Covers web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts and web/src/app/api/v1/freebuff/session/_handlers.ts. Production unreachable because Cloudflare always sets cf-ipcountry.

eli5.text: Developers running the app on their own computers can now test the free-tier access gate locally: requests coming from their machine (like 127.0.0.1) are treated as US-allowed when the environment is marked as dev, so they don't need a real country lookup. In production, this path is never used because Cloudflare always supplies a country code. The feature only applies when the local dev flag is set; if your machine isn't marked that way, nothing changes for you. This is already live in the codebase, so developers with the right flag can bypass the country check right now.

ai.title: Revert Kimi K2.6 to GLM 5.1 in free and lite agents
ai.summary: Reverts the recent switch to MoonshotAI Kimi K2.6, restoring Z.AI GLM 5.1 as the default model for free and lite agent modes. The change updates `FREEBUFF_MODELS` constants, CLI selector logic, and agent definitions (`base2`, `editor-lite`, `code-reviewer-lite`) to use `z-ai/glm-5.1`. `moonshotai/kimi-k2.6` is removed from `ModelName` types and free agent model sets. Existing sessions and saved preferences referencing Kimi are unaffected by this config-level revert, but new sessions will default to GLM 5.1.

eli5.text: The free coding mode switched back to using the GLM 5.1 assistant instead of the Kimi K2.6 assistant. If you use the free or lite mode of the coding tool, you are now talking to GLM 5.1 again instead of Kimi K2.6. The program tried Kimi briefly, then reverted to GLM 5.1 as the default for these free modes. Anyone who had picked a different model and saved that preference still sees their saved choice the next time they open the tool.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.53 release packages country gating harden, Kimi tool
ai.summary: Version 0.0.53 rolls up a day of user-visible work into a single release bump in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`. The waiting room now fails closed on unresolved IPs via `ip_privacy_lookup_failed` and new `free_session` columns in migration `0047_tough_silver_fox.sql`, the `moonshotai/*` adapters inject required `id`/`name` fields through `kimi-tool-compat.ts`, and ad payloads normalize to `ads: AdResponse[] | null` across CLI and Web. The default free/lite model also reverts to `z-ai/glm-5.1` after a same-day swap to `moonshotai/kimi-k2.6`, while a dev-only `allowLocalhost` bypass lets loopback requests skip country checks during local development.
ai.evidence: The diff to `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` only changes the `version` field from `0.0.52` to `0.0.53`; the release is labeled a version bump packaging accumulated changes.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.53 rolls out stronger geography-based access controls and adds support for MoonshotAI's Kimi models so they work smoothly with tool-calling features. The app now blocks sessions more strictly when a user's location can't be determined or is restricted for privacy reasons, recording detailed reasons for each block and protecting user privacy by hashing IP addresses. Kimi models are now compatible with the system's tool calling, meaning they receive the proper identifiers and formatting required without users having to adjust anything manually. The default free 'Smartest' model was briefly switched to Kimi K2.6 and then reverted back to Z.AI GLM 5.1, so free and lite users continue using the same familiar default as before. Ads shown to users are also simplified, returning a cleaner list format across the CLI and web, and developers running local tests will find the country check automatically bypassed on localhost so they can test without being incorrectly blocked. Upgrading gives you more reliable regional access handling, better model compatibility, and a smoother, more consistent experience whether you are chatting, coding, or just browsing.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI 1.0.645 release
ai.summary: Bumped the Freebuff CLI release package version from 1.0.644 to 1.0.645 in `cli/release/package.json`, packaging the day's accumulated changes including the Kimi tool call compatibility layer for `moonshotai/*` models, simplified `ads: AdResponse[] | null` ad response shape across CLI and Web, and the revert restoring `z-ai/glm-5.1` as the default free and lite agent model. The change is a pure version bump in the release manifest with no functional code modifications; all user-visible features, model routing, country gating, and CLI waiting room improvements referenced in the release notes shipped as separate commits earlier in the same-day sequence. Affected packages span `cli/`, `web/`, `common/`, and `packages/agent-runtime/`, with migration SQL `0047_tough_silver_fox.sql` and bot sweep scripts included in the broader release.
ai.evidence: Commit 1efa3316 modifies only `cli/release/package.json`, bumping the version field from `1.0.644` to `1.0.645`. The diff is a single line change in the release packaging manifest with no functional code changes. This is a release-bump commit within the same-day sequence that includes the Kimi tool call compat layer, ad response shape simplification, GLM 5.1/Kimi K2.6 model swaps, country blocking, and other Freebuff waiting room improvements.

eli5.text: This release upgrades your free AI coding experience with better model options, stronger bot protection, and clearer waiting-room controls. You can now switch between available AI models directly while waiting in the free queue, and the CLI remembers your choice instead of silently re-queuing you to a random model. The default free model switched to MoonshotAI Kimi K2.6 (with GLM 5.1 as a fallback during limited hours), and banned or abusive accounts are blocked faster with hourly sweeps and instant IP-VPN detection. You'll also see more accurate queue positions, better ad choices in the wait screen, and the waiting room now shows specific reasons (like VPN or Tor blocks) instead of generic errors. Upgrading means fewer surprise model switches, cleaner navigation with Tab and arrow keys, and a smoother path back to model selection after each session ends.

ai.title: Subagent tool names use underscores
ai.summary: Direct subagent tool names now use underscores (e.g., `code_searcher`) instead of hyphens, driven by new `getAgentToolName` helper in `packages/agent-runtime/src/templates/prompts.ts`. This aligns tool identifiers with provider-native expectations and resolves potential schema compatibility issues. The change impacts `common/src/tools/params/tool/spawn-agents.ts` and `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts`. `getAgentShortName` remains for internal ID mapping, while `toolSet` keys in `buildAgentToolSet` and execution lookups now consume the underscored variant.

eli5.text: When the assistant asks helper agents to do things like search code, it now calls them by name using underscores (for example, code_searcher) instead of hyphens. This matters for you only if you watch the assistant's internal tool calls, because the names it sends to those helper agents now match what the underlying AI providers expect, so calls that used to risk being misread will now line up correctly. The old internal nicknames for these agents are still used behind the scenes for bookkeeping, but the names that actually leave the assistant and reach the helper agents now use underscores everywhere they are listed and when results come back.
